front: Which graph traversal guarantees the shortest path (by edge count) in an unweighted graph?
BFS uses which data structure to track what to visit next? DFS?
back: BFS uses a queue (FIFO). DFS uses a stack (LIFO), often implicit via recursion.

front: Time complexity of both BFS and DFS?
back: Θ(V + E) — every vertex visited once, every edge examined once (twice for undirected graphs).

front: Adjacency list vs. adjacency matrix: space complexity of each?
back: Adjacency list: Θ(V+E), good for sparse graphs. Adjacency matrix: Θ(V²), O(1) edge lookup but wasteful for sparse graphs.

front: What graph structure is topological sort only defined for?
back: A DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph) — a cycle makes a consistent 'before/after' ordering impossible.

front: How does DFS-based topological sort build the ordering?
back: Each time a vertex finishes (all its descendants processed), insert it at the FRONT of a linked list. Θ(V+E) total.

front: Which edge types can appear in an UNDIRECTED graph's DFS? Which can't?
back: Only tree edges and back edges are possible — forward and cross edges can't occur, since every edge is encountered from both endpoints.

front: SCC algorithm: what are the three main steps?
back: 1) DFS(G) to get finish times. 2) Compute the transpose graph Gᵀ (reverse all edges). 3) DFS(Gᵀ) visiting vertices in descending finish-time order — each resulting DFS tree is one SCC.
